Verifying tokens against a JWKS

Source: vignettes/articles/jwks-resolver.Rmd
jwks-resolver.Rmd

An OpenID Connect provider signs its tokens with keys it publishes as a JWK Set (JWKS), and it rotates them: a new key appears in the set before the first token signed with it, and an old key stays until its tokens expire. A client has to fetch that set, cache it, and fetch it again when a token names a key it has not seen.

zujose never fetches anything itself. Every function that checks a token takes, instead of a key, a resolver: a function of the token’s header that returns a key or a key set. This article writes one with httr2.

library(zujose)

A resolver is a function of the header

The resolver gets the token’s header, a named list, before anything is verified. It may read kid, alg or iss from it to choose keys. What it returns is still checked: the key must fit one of the algorithms you allowed, and the signature must verify with it.

current <- jwk_generate("EC", crv = "P-256", alg = "ES256", kid = "2026-11")
provider_keys <- jwk_set(current)

resolver <- function(header) {
  message("resolving kid ", header$kid)
  jwk_public(provider_keys)
}

jwt <- jwt_encode(
  list(iss = "https://auth.example", aud = "orders-api"),
  current,
  expires_in = 600
)
jwt_decode(jwt, resolver, algorithms = "ES256", audience = "orders-api")$iss
#> resolving kid 2026-11
#> [1] "https://auth.example"

Because the header is untrusted, never let it decide where keys come from. A jku or x5u URL in a header is ignored by zujose, and a resolver should only follow one that is on an allow-list you wrote.

Fetching and caching the JWKS

The provider’s discovery document, at <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration, gives the URL of its JWKS as jwks_uri. The resolver below fetches the set once, keeps it for ttl seconds, and fetches it again early when a token names a kid the cached set does not have, but at most once every min_refresh seconds, so a flood of tokens with made-up kids cannot turn it into a flood of requests.

jwks_resolver <- function(issuer, ttl = 3600, min_refresh = 60) {
  cache <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())

  fetch <- function() {
    config <- httr2::request(issuer) |>
      httr2::req_url_path_append(".well-known", "openid-configuration") |>
      httr2::req_perform() |>
      httr2::resp_body_json()
    if (!identical(config$issuer, issuer)) {
      stop("The discovery document is for another issuer.")
    }
    jwks <- httr2::request(config$jwks_uri) |>
      httr2::req_perform() |>
      httr2::resp_body_string()
    cache$keys <- as_jwk_set(jwks)
    cache$fetched <- Sys.time()
  }

  has_kid <- function(kid) {
    tryCatch(
      {
        cache$keys[[kid]]
        TRUE
      },
      zujose_key_error = function(e) FALSE
    )
  }

  function(header) {
    age <- if (is.null(cache$fetched)) {
      Inf
    } else {
      as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), cache$fetched, units = "secs"))
    }
    stale <- age > ttl
    unknown <- !is.null(header$kid) && !is.null(cache$keys) &&
      !has_kid(header$kid)
    if (stale || (unknown && age > min_refresh)) {
      fetch()
    }
    cache$keys
  }
}

Build the resolver once, when the app starts, and give it to jwt_decoder() with the rest of the policy. Every call then shares one cache:

check <- jwt_decoder(
  key = jwks_resolver("https://accounts.google.com"),
  algorithms = "RS256",
  issuer = "https://accounts.google.com",
  audience = "my-client-id.apps.googleusercontent.com"
)

claims <- check(id_token)

The cached keys are public, so the cache holds no secrets. A JWKS can list keys zujose cannot use, such as Ed25519 keys; they are kept in the set and skipped when a token does not name them.

Several issuers

A service that accepts tokens from more than one provider can read iss from the payload with jose_peek(), pick that provider’s resolver, and then check the token against it. The issuer check inside jwt_decode() makes sure the token really came from the issuer whose keys were used:

resolvers <- list(
  "https://accounts.google.com" = jwks_resolver("https://accounts.google.com"),
  "https://login.example.org" = jwks_resolver("https://login.example.org")
)

check_token <- function(token) {
  iss <- jose_peek(token)$claims$iss
  if (!is.character(iss) || !iss %in% names(resolvers)) {
    stop("Unknown issuer.")
  }
  jwt_decode(
    token,
    resolvers[[iss]],
    algorithms = c("RS256", "ES256"),
    issuer = iss,
    audience = "orders-api"
  )
}
